about.heading: About
about.studyOnly: OpenRange is a study tool. It does not read your screen, show overlays or HUDs, or connect to any poker site. Hand-history import is for reviewing sessions after you play.
about.offline: Everything runs on this device. There are no accounts, no telemetry, and no network requests after the app has loaded.
about.milestone: This is an early build: the equity calculator works; drills, charts and lessons arrive in later milestones.
equity.heading: Equity calculator
equity.intro: Equity is your share of the pot if all the cards are dealt out with no more betting, counting a split pot as half. Enter a hand (AhKh) or a range (QQ+, AKs, T9s-54s) for each player.
equity.exactNote: Exact: all {runouts} ways to complete the board were checked for every possible matchup (no sampling error).
equity.mcNote: Estimate from {samples} random deals (seed {seed}). The ± value is one standard error: the true equity is within about two of them 95% of the time.
solver.heading: Postflop solver
solver.intro: Solve a heads-up flop, turn or river spot on this device. OOP (out of position) acts first. Bet sizes are percentages of the pot; raise sizes are percentages of the pot after calling; 'a' means all-in. River spots solve in seconds; turn spots in seconds to a minute; flop spots can take many minutes in the browser, so start with small trees.
solver.allIn: All-in if a bet uses ≥ this % of stack
solver.cancelled: Cancelled. The solver's memory was freed.
solver.info: Memory estimate {mb} MB · {oop} OOP hands · {ip} IP hands · {nodes} game nodes
solver.progress: Iteration {iterations} · exploitability {pct}% of pot ({bb} bb) at the last check · {seconds} s
solver.badge: Solved on this device · {algorithm} · {iterations} iterations · exploitability {pct}% of pot
solver.hitMax: Stopped at the iteration limit before reaching the target; the strategy is less accurate.
lock.lockedSummary: This node is locked: change or unlock it
lock.intro: Fix this player's strategy here and re-solve: everything else becomes the best play against it. Presets start from the solved strategy and shift its frequencies hand by hand.
lock.amount: Share of the other actions moved
lock.listNote: The solve is now the best response to these locks; its exploitability measures how far it is from that, with the locked choices fixed.
lock.evChange: EV with the locks: OOP {oop} bb, IP {ip} bb (before locking: OOP {oop0} bb, IP {ip0} bb).
solver.opponentRange: {who}'s range at this node: {combos} combos (bar height: how much of each hand is left).
runouts.summary: Runout explorer: the next decision for every card
runouts.intro: For each card, how often {who} takes each action at the next decision (range-weighted). Click a card to go there.
painter.summary: Paint the ranges on a grid
painter.how: Click a hand to add or remove it; the range text updates. Hands with a partial weight count as in when half or more.
solver.pickCell: Pick a hand in the grid to see each combo's strategy and EV.
solver.notInRange: {hand} isn't in the range at this point.
solver.evNote: EV is in big blinds, measured from the start of this spot (pot winnings minus chips put in on this street). Compare actions within a row; actions a solver mixes between have almost equal EV.
solver.simplify: If the spot doesn't fit the memory budget, simplify the tree automatically (you'll see exactly what changed)
solver.symmetries: Suit symmetry lets {n} equivalent card choices share one computation.
solver.abstractionHeading: Simplified to fit the memory budget:
solver.abstractionNote: The solution is for this simpler game tree, not the one you entered. Results for removed options are not available.
solver.badgeSimplified: Solved on this device (simplified tree) · {algorithm} · {iterations} iterations · exploitability {pct}% of pot
solver.chanceHeader: Deal the {street} card · board so far {board}
solver.alsoStandsFor: Also stands for {cards} (same situation with suits relabelled)
solver.isoNote: Cards marked +N stand for N more cards that are the same situation with the suits relabelled; the solver computes them once.
solver.estimate: This spot needs about {mb} MB as entered.
charts.heading: Preflop charts
charts.intro: Each chart shows, for one decision, how often each starting hand takes each action. Split cells are mixed strategies: both actions have (almost) the same EV, so either is fine. Pick a hand to see the EV of each action. Every chart says where its numbers come from.
charts.none: No charts have been generated yet (run solver-cli gen-charts).
charts.legend: Actions and how often they are taken
charts.exactNote: Solved to an exploitability of {ex} bb per hand.
charts.approxWarning: These charts come from an approximate model. Push/fold charts for 3+ players are solved by sampling, and CFR with several players isn't guaranteed to find an equilibrium; cash-game charts also replace postflop play with an equity-realization model. Use them as a guide, not as exact answers.
charts.bandHeading: Outside the sanity checks: don't study these as reference yet.
charts.bandNote: Known cause: the equity-realization model (v1) gives weak hands the same realization as strong ones, so the blinds defend too wide and late positions open too tight.
charts.bandNoteV2: These charts use equity realization measured per hand from OpenRange's own postflop solves (EQR v2). What is still approximate: the simplified preflop tree, the small postflop tree used for the measurement, sampling error in the measured factors, and measurement at 100 bb only. See Known limits.
charts.notReached: {hand} never gets to this decision with this strategy, so there is nothing to show.
charts.reach: This hand reaches this decision {pct} of the time when dealt (because of your own earlier choices).
charts.pickCell: Pick a hand in the grid to see its frequencies and the EV of each action.
charts.evNote: EV in {unit}. Within one hand, compare actions: the difference is how much a choice costs.
pushfold.heading: Push/fold calculator (heads-up decision, chip EV or ICM)
pushfold.intro: Everyone else has folded. One player moves all-in or folds; the other calls or folds. The solver finds the exact equilibrium for these two decisions over all 1326 starting hands, with exact card removal. With payouts it uses ICM (Malmuth–Harville) on the whole table, so the other players' stacks matter too.
pushfold.stacksHint: Every player still in the tournament, e.g. 12, 20, 8.
pushfold.pusher: Seat that shoves (usually the small blind)
pushfold.caller: Seat that calls (usually the big blind)
pushfold.badge: Exact for this model · computed on this device · {iterations} iterations
pushfold.note: Model: blinds 0.5/1; only these two players' decisions are solved (everyone else folds); a player who busts takes the lowest remaining prize, shared equally if two bust at once. EVs are in bb (chip EV) or in prize units (ICM) and include what each player already posted.
trainer.heading: Trainer
trainer.intro: Answer spots and get graded by how much EV your choice gives up compared with the best play, in big blinds (preflop) or % of the pot (postflop). Hands from the solution's mix are never marked wrong. Spots you miss come back sooner.
trainer.verdict.bestTie: {chosen} is one of the best plays (tied with {others}).
trainer.verdict.mixed: {chosen} is part of the solution's mix: it is played {freq} of the time. The solution plays {top} more often, but at equilibrium both earn the same.
trainer.verdict.inMix: {chosen} is the solution's main play with this hand ({freq} of the time).
trainer.verdict.allowance: These EVs are sampled, so the loss that counts after allowing for sampling error is {graded}.
trainer.verdict.unconverged: The EVs inside this mix still differ by {loss}, so the solution isn't fully converged for this hand.
trainer.mix: The solution's mix for this hand: {list}.
trainer.sampled: This reference is solved by sampling: EVs carry standard errors (largest ±{se} bb).
trainer.practice: Practice spot: this chart is outside its sanity checks, so the answer isn't graded and doesn't count in your stats or review schedule.
trainer.callMath: Calling costs {toCall} bb more to win a pot of {pot} bb, so you need {required} equity. Against the hands that shove, yours has {equity}.
trainer.callMath.continue: So calling earns {diff} more than folding.
trainer.callMath.fold: So folding saves {diff} compared with calling.
trainer.callMath.even: So calling and folding are about break-even.
trainer.shoveMath: If you shove, the big blind folds {fold} of the time (you win the 1 bb blind) and calls otherwise, when your hand has {eqCalled} equity. Together, shoving is worth {evShove} against {evFold} for folding.
trainer.shoveMath.neverCalled: If you shove, the big blind always folds and you win the 1 bb blind: shoving is worth {evShove} against {evFold} for folding.
trainer.lesson: Related lesson: {title} (lessons arrive in a later update).
trainer.nextHint: Press Enter or N for the next hand. Action keys: F fold, C check/call, R bet/raise/all-in, or the number of the button.
trainer.pf.sbFirst: You are in the small blind. What do you do?
trainer.pf.bbVsShove: The small blind moves all-in for {stack} bb. You are in the big blind. What do you do?
trainer.pf.firstToAct: Everyone before you has folded or you are first to act.
trainer.filters.none: No spots match these filters. Widen them to keep drilling.
trainer.filters.practiceNote: Cash charts are practice only: they're outside their sanity checks.
trainer.answer.heading: Result
trainer.answer.combo: Graded by hand class ({hand}): the chart doesn't distinguish suits.
trainer.saveError: Your answer couldn't be saved on this device: {message}
trainer.session: This session: {n} answered, average EV loss {loss}.
trainer.verdict.mixNoise: In the solver's numbers the actions in this mix differ by {loss}, which is within its convergence accuracy.
trainer.verdict.withinNoise: {best} measured {loss} better, but that's within the reference's sampling error, so your answer counts as Best.
trainer.verdict.tiny: {best} is better by only {loss}, small enough that your answer counts as Best.
trainer.accuracy: Reference: this spot was solved in your browser to an exploitability of {x}% of the pot.
trainer.offPath: Not graded: with this hand the solution almost never gets here (it reaches this point {share} as often as it holds the hand), so its numbers aren't a reliable reference.
trainer.potOdds: Calling costs {toCall} bb to win a pot of {pot} bb, so you need {required} equity. Against the hands the opponent plays this way, yours has {equity}.
trainer.potOdds.even: Calling and folding are about break-even.
trainer.potOdds.raw: Before the river, this price check only uses your equity right now: both players can still bet later, so the solver's EVs below decide.
trainer.potOdds.disagree: Here the simple check and the solver disagree, because of the betting still to come.
trainer.mdf: Against this bet, a defender who doesn't want any two cards to profit as a bluff must continue with at least {mdf} of their range. The solution continues with {defend} of yours here.
trainer.spr: Stack-to-pot ratio {spr}: {stack} bb behind with {pot} bb in the pot.
trainer.texture.rainbow: no two cards of one suit
trainer.advantage: Your range has {equity} equity against the opponent's here ({lead}). {heroNuts} of your range and {villainNuts} of theirs are very strong (at least {nut} equity).
trainer.advantage.villain: the opponent has the range advantage
trainer.advantage.even: neither side has a clear range advantage
trainer.blockers: Your cards remove {strong} of the opponent's strong hands (at least 70% equity against your range) and {weak} of their weak ones (30% or less).
trainer.post.intro: Pick a spot. It is solved once in your browser; then you play hands against the solution. The opponent plays the solved strategy with its real cards, and each of your decisions is graded in % of the pot.
trainer.post.inputs: Ranges and bet sizes are example inputs (the same as on the Solver page); the strategy is solved here.

trainer.post.solving: Solving… {it} iterations, exploitability {x}% of the pot
trainer.post.ready: Solved to {x}% of the pot in {s} s ({it} iterations).
trainer.post.notReached: The solve stopped at {x}% of the pot, above its {target}% target: grades allow for that.
trainer.post.error: The solver stopped with an error: {message}
review.empty: No answers yet. Drill a few spots and your stats appear here.
review.summary: {n} answers on this device: {graded} graded, {practice} practice or not graded.
review.unit.pctPot: Postflop (EV loss in % of the pot)
review.leakNote: A group is marked as a leak only when its average EV loss interval lies entirely above the interval of all your other answers. Groups with fewer than {min} graded answers show no numbers.
review.scheduleSummary: {families} spot families seen; {due} due now; next one due {next}.
review.settingsNote: Upper bounds of Best, Acceptable, Inaccuracy and Mistake (anything above is a Blunder). Defaults are documented in DECISIONS D-052. Changing them affects new answers only.
review.invalid: Thresholds must be positive and increasing.
review.dataNote: Everything is stored only in this browser on this device. Nothing is sent anywhere.

widget.cardsHint: Type cards like "Ah Kd 7c": rank (A K Q J T 9 … 2) then suit (s h d c). A hand needs 5 to 7 cards.
widget.outsHint: Give two cards each and a flop (3 cards) or turn (4 cards), all different.
widget.tie: It's a tie: the pot is split.
widget.outs.ahead: You are not behind right now; these are the cards that keep you ahead.
widget.outs.count: Cards that put you ahead on the next card: {n} of {of}.
widget.outs.nextCard: Chance on the very next card: {p}.
widget.outs.rule4: Rule of 4 (two cards to come): {n} outs × 4 ≈ {est}.
widget.outs.rule2: Rule of 2 (one card to come): {n} outs × 2 ≈ {est}.
widget.outs.exact: Exact equity by the end, counting every runout: {eq}.
widget.combos.known: Cards you can see (yours, the board)
widget.combos.count: {left} of the {total} combos of {hand} are still possible.
widget.potodds.steps: You call {bet} bb to win the pot plus the bet: the pot will be {pot} + {bet} + {bet} = {final} bb.
widget.potodds.required: You need at least {required} equity to call.
widget.potodds.enough: With {eq} equity the call pays on this simple check.
widget.potodds.short: With {eq} equity you are short of the price on this simple check.
widget.potodds.caveat: This ignores future betting (implied odds) and assumes you see the end of the hand.
widget.ev.total: EV = sum of the last column = {ev} bb.
widget.ev.sum: The probabilities add up to {total}, not 1: check them.
widget.spr.potBets: Pot-sized bets needed to get all the money in: {n}.
widget.sizing.alpha: Folds a pure bluff needs to break even
widget.sizing.bluffs: Bluffs in a balanced river betting range
widget.sizing.caveat: These are simple river models: one bet, no raises, a range of strong hands and bluffs.
widget.chart.approx: Approximate model: see the badge for how it was made.
widget.chart.outOfBand: This chart set is outside some sanity checks: treat it as a rough guide.
widget.toy.setup: River on K♥9♦6♣3♠2♥, pot {pot} bb. The bettor has a set of nines (value) or Q-J (air, never wins at showdown); the caller has A-K, which beats Q-J and loses to the set. The bettor checks or goes all-in for the bet below; the caller calls or folds.
widget.toy.solved: Solved by the engine to {x}% of the pot in {it} iterations.
widget.toy.formulas: Theory: with enough air, bluffs are B ÷ (P + 2B) of the bets and the caller calls P ÷ (P + B), the minimum defence frequency. With too little air, every air hand bluffs and the caller folds. Results are bb won from the pot per hand.
widget.toy.lock: Lock the caller: calls this often
widget.toy.brAll: Best response: bluff with all your air.
widget.toy.brNone: Best response: don't bluff at all.
widget.toy.brAny: Every bluffing frequency earns the same: the caller is at the MDF.
widget.toy.brEv: The bettor's best response earns {br} per hand, against {eq} at equilibrium: a difference of {gain}.
widget.toy.brNote: Computed from the game's rules: a bluff wins the pot when the caller folds and loses the bet when called; value hands win the pot plus the call.
widget.icm.bubble: If {caller} calls: prize equity {now} now, {win} after winning, {lose} after losing. Bubble factor {factor}: losing costs that many times what winning gains, so the call needs {needed} equity (50.0% in chips).
widget.icm.note: ICM (Malmuth–Harville): each player's chance of finishing first is their share of the chips, and so on for the next places. It ignores skill, position and blinds.
widget.variance.behind: Chance of being behind at the end
widget.variance.ruin: Chance of ever losing {bankroll} bb (risk of ruin)
widget.variance.sim: {n} simulated players with these numbers: {behind} finish behind; the worst fall from a high point was {worst} bb.
widget.variance.note: Results are approximated as normal in blocks of 100 hands; risk of ruin uses the standard formula exp(−2 × win rate × bankroll ÷ SD²). The simulation is seeded, so it shows the same paths each time.
widget.chart.pick: Click or tap a cell to see its frequencies and EVs.
widget.chart.evNote: EVs are in bb from the start of the hand and are estimated by sampling; ± is two standard errors. Differences inside that margin are noise.
widget.advantage.nuts: Very strong hands (85% equity or more): {share}
widget.advantage.spread: Spread of equities across the range
widget.table.label: A 6-max poker table: button, small blind, big blind, UTG, hijack, cutoff.
widget.table.note: The button (D) moves one seat clockwise every hand. The two seats after it post the blinds.
widget.flow.split: Same hand: the pot is split.
widget.flow.blinds.name: Blinds
widget.flow.blinds.text: Before any cards, the two players after the button post the blinds: forced bets that give everyone something to play for.
widget.flow.deal.name: Deal
widget.flow.deal.text: Everyone gets two private cards, the hole cards.
widget.flow.preflop.name: Preflop
widget.flow.preflop.text: First betting round, starting with the player after the big blind.
widget.flow.flop.name: Flop
widget.flow.flop.text: Three shared cards are dealt face up, then a betting round starting after the button.
widget.flow.turn.name: Turn
widget.flow.turn.text: A fourth shared card, then another betting round.
widget.flow.river.name: River
widget.flow.river.text: The fifth and last shared card, then the last betting round.
widget.flow.showdown.name: Showdown
widget.flow.showdown.text: If two or more players are left, they show their cards; the best five-card hand wins.
math.potodds.q: The pot is {pot} bb and your opponent bets {bet} bb. What equity do you need to call?
math.potodds.s1: You call {bet} bb. If you call, the pot will be {pot} + {bet} + {bet} = {final} bb.
math.potodds.s2: Price = your call ÷ the final pot = {bet} ÷ {final} = {answer}.
math.mdf.q: The pot is {pot} bb and your opponent bets {bet} bb. What is the minimum defence frequency?
math.mdf.s1: A pure bluff risks {bet} to win {pot}; it breaks even if you fold {bet} ÷ ({pot} + {bet}) = {alpha} of the time.
math.mdf.s2: So you must continue with at least {pot} ÷ ({pot} + {bet}) = {answer} of your range to stop any two cards from profiting.
math.bluff.q: On the river you bet {bet} bb into {pot} bb with a range of strong hands and bluffs. What share of your betting range can be bluffs, so that a call breaks even?
math.bluff.s1: The caller pays {bet} to win {pot} + {bet} + {bet}: their price is {price}.
math.bluff.s2: Bluffs should be {answer} of your bets (and value hands {value}), about {ratio} value bets for each bluff.
math.texture.s.rainbow: Three different suits: rainbow, no flush draw yet.
math.texture.s.twotone: Two cards share a suit: two-tone, flush draws are possible.
math.texture.s.monotone: All three cards share a suit: monotone, a flush is already possible.
math.texture.s.paired: Two cards share a rank: paired, so trips and full houses are possible.
math.texture.s.unpaired: No two cards share a rank: unpaired.
math.texture.s.straight: Three ranks fit within five in a row, so two hole cards can make a straight.
math.texture.s.noStraight: No three ranks fit within five in a row, so no straight is possible yet.
math.reading.q: Your opponent's bet means {a} or {b} (nothing else). Which is more likely?
math.reading.s1: {hand}: {total} combos in a full deck, {left} left after the cards you can see.
math.reading.s2: {more} is more likely, by about {ratio} to 1.
math.reading.s2same: They have the same number of combos left, so they are equally likely.
math.combos.q: You can see {known}. How many combos of {hand} can your opponent still have?
math.combos.s1: {hand} has {total} combos before you look at any cards.
math.combos.s2: {removed} of them use a card you can see, so {left} are left.
math.outs.q: You know your opponent's hand. How many cards put you ahead on the turn?
math.outs.s2: Rule of 4 with two cards to come: {outs} × 4 ≈ {estimate}.
math.outs.s3: The exact equity, counting every turn and river: {exact}.
math.equity.q: Both hands go all-in before the flop. Roughly how much equity does your hand have?
math.equity.s1: Exactly {exact} over all boards, which is in the {band} band.

onboarding.title: Welcome to OpenRange
onboarding.intro: Three quick choices so the app fits you. You can change everything later in Settings.
onboarding.experience: How much poker do you know?
onboarding.exp.new.hint: Start from the rules; extra help everywhere.
onboarding.exp.experienced.hint: Solver terms are fine; show me everything.
onboarding.modeNote: New and basics start in Guided mode (plain words, hints, simpler screens); experienced starts in Expert mode. Switch any time from the top bar. Modes change how things are shown, never the answers.
settings.presetsNote: Presets change how much help and detail you see. They never change grading or the solver.
settings.gameNote: Defaults for the workbench and for play mode (M9). Drills always use the structure of their reference chart or spot, and say so.
settings.theme.help: Follow your system, or always dark or light.
settings.palette.help: The colour-blind palette (Okabe–Ito) stays distinct with the common kinds of colour blindness. Actions always also have a symbol and a label.
settings.deck.help: Four colours give every suit its own colour, which makes flushes easier to see.
settings.cardBack.help: Design on the back of face-down cards.
settings.units.help: Show stacks and bets in big blinds, or in chips (1 bb = 100 chips).
settings.animation.help: Dealing, chips and panels. Off removes animation completely.
settings.reduceMotion.help: System follows your device's reduce-motion setting, which turns animation off.
settings.textSize.help: Scales all text and the layout around it.
settings.density.help: Compact fits more on the screen.
settings.sound.help: Soft sounds for dealing and answers. Off by default.
settings.hints.help: Offer step-by-step hints you can reveal before you answer. Using one is noted but doesn't count against you.
settings.autoAdvance.help: Move to the next hand by itself a moment after the feedback (study mode waits for you).
settings.timer.help: Optional time limit per decision. Running out just shows the answer; nothing is graded.
settings.srs.help: How soon spots you've got right come back: light spaces them out more, intense brings them back sooner.
settings.detail.help: How many reasons the coach gives after each answer.
settings.showMath.help: EVs, the full mix, equity and the price, opened automatically.
settings.liveCoach.help: Coaching during hands in play mode (M9); otherwise only after the hand.
settings.gameType.help: Cash games value chips directly; tournaments use ICM near the money.
settings.ante.help: Per-player ante in big blinds; 0 for none.
settings.rake.help: A share of each pot the house takes, with a cap.
settings.algorithm.help: DCFR is the validated default and converges fastest here; CFR+ is offered for comparison.
settings.maxIterations.help: The solver stops after this many iterations even if the target isn't reached.
settings.targetPct.help: The solver stops once a perfect opponent could gain at most this much. Lower is more accurate and slower.
settings.memoryMb.help: Largest spot the browser solver will build. Spots that don't fit are simplified (if allowed) or refused.
settings.simplify.help: Drop bet sizes or raises (and say exactly which) instead of refusing a spot over the memory limit.
settings.threads.fixed: The browser solver runs on one thread (D-010); the command-line solver uses all cores.
settings.memoryEstimate: The example flop spot needs about {mb} MB; your limit is {limit} MB.
settings.memoryNoFit: It would be simplified or refused.
coach.verdict.best.2: Spot on: {chosen} is the best play.
coach.verdict.mixed.1: Fine: this is a close spot played two ways. {top} is slightly more common.
coach.verdict.mixed.2: Good: the solver plays this hand two ways, and {chosen} is one of them. {top} is slightly more common.
coach.verdict.close: Fine, close call: {best} is a hair better (about {loss}).
coach.verdict.acceptable: Fine, close call: {best} is a little better (about {loss}).
coach.verdict.inaccuracy: Small mistake: {best} is better; this costs about {loss}.
coach.verdict.mistake: Mistake: {best} is better; this costs about {loss}.
coach.verdict.blunder: Big mistake: {best} is much better; this costs about {loss}.
coach.verdict.offPath: Not graded: the solution almost never reaches this point with your hand.
coach.verdict.practice: Not graded: practice chart (outside its sanity checks).
coach.verdict.noReference: Not graded: no solved reference for this line.
coach.why.offPath: With this hand the solution gets here only {share} as often as it holds it, so its numbers here aren't a reliable guide.
coach.why.practice: This chart is approximate and outside its sanity checks, so it's shown for reference only.
coach.why.price: You pay {toCall} bb to play for a pot of {pot} bb, so you need {required} equity.
coach.why.equityVsShove: Against the hands that shove, yours has {equity}: {verdict}.
coach.why.equityVsRange: Against the hands that bet like this, yours has {equity}.
coach.why.futureBetting: The simple price check and the solver disagree here because there's more betting to come.
coach.why.alwaysFolds: The big blind folds to this shove every time, so you just win the blind.
coach.why.foldEquity: The big blind folds {fold} of the time, which wins you the blind; when called, you have {equity} equity.
coach.why.shoveTotal: Put together, shoving is worth {shove} against {fold} for folding.
coach.why.mix: This is a close spot: the solver plays it {a} {pa} and {b} {pb}, and both earn about the same.
coach.why.behind: From the {seat}, {n} players still act after you, and any of them can wake up with a strong hand.
coach.why.hand.pair: {hand} is a pocket pair: it's already made, but it rarely improves.
coach.why.hand.suited: {hand} is suited, which adds flush chances and makes it easier to play after the flop.
coach.why.hand.offsuit: {hand} is offsuit, so it has fewer ways to make strong hands than its suited version.
coach.why.advantage.hero: Your range is ahead of theirs on this board (about {equity} equity), which supports betting.
coach.why.advantage.villain: Their range is ahead of yours on this board (you have about {equity}), so be careful.
coach.why.advantage.even: Neither range is clearly ahead on this board (you have about {equity}).
coach.why.mdf: To stop any two cards from bluffing profitably you'd defend {mdf}; the solution defends {defend} of your range.
coach.why.blocksValue: Your cards remove more of their strong hands ({strong}) than their weak ones ({weak}), which helps a bluff or a call.
coach.why.blocksBluffs: Your cards remove more of their weak hands ({weak}) than their strong ones ({strong}), which makes a call or bluff a bit worse.
coach.wet: coordinated (flushes or straights are possible), so hands change a lot on later streets
coach.dry: dry: few draws, so hands rarely change
coach.idea.potOdds.1: Compare the price with your equity against the hands that bet, not against a random hand.
coach.idea.potOdds.2: A call needs equity at least equal to the price: what you pay divided by the final pot.
coach.idea.pushFold.1: Short-stacked, folds win the blinds often enough that many hands profit even when they're called.
coach.idea.pushFold.2: A shove wins two ways: the opponent folds, or you win the all-in.
coach.idea.mixed.1: When the solver mixes, both options are fine: pick one and keep going.
coach.idea.mixed.2: Mixed spots are close by definition; save your attention for clear decisions.
coach.idea.ranges.1: The earlier your position, the more players can still wake up with a hand, so open fewer hands.
coach.idea.ranges.2: Position matters: hands that are fine on the button can lose money from early seats.
coach.idea.postflop.1: Think about both ranges, not just your hand: who has more strong hands on this board?
coach.idea.postflop.2: Good postflop play starts with the price, the board and who is ahead.
coach.look.potOdds: the bet size: work out the price before you decide.
coach.look.pushFold: your stack depth and how often the next player calls.
coach.look.mixed: whether a spot is a close one: if both actions are in the mix, either is fine.
coach.look.ranges: how many players are still to act after you.
coach.look.postflop: the board texture and which range it favours.
coach.math.wrong: Not quite: you answered {given}; the answer is {answer}.
coach.math.idea.potodds: Price = what you pay ÷ the pot you'll have after calling.
coach.math.idea.mdf: Defend at least pot ÷ (pot + bet), or any two cards can bluff you.
coach.math.idea.bluff: On the river your bluffs can be as large a share of your bets as the caller's price.
coach.math.idea.outs: Rule of 4 on the flop, 2 on the turn, then check it against the exact number.
coach.math.idea.equity: Pairs and dominating hands do best all-in; most other matchups are closer than they look.
coach.math.idea.combos: Pairs have 6 combos, suited hands 4, offsuit 12; every card you can see removes some.
coach.math.idea.texture: Read a flop by suits, pairs and connectedness: together they say which draws and strong hands exist.
coach.math.idea.reading: Count combos before you fear a hand: what you can see removes many of them.
coach.math.look.potodds: the final pot: it includes your call.
coach.math.look.mdf: the pot before the bet, not after.
coach.math.look.bluff: the bet as a share of the final pot.
coach.math.look.outs: outs that also help the opponent: they don't count.
coach.math.look.equity: whether one hand dominates the other (a shared card).
coach.math.look.texture: three ranks within five in a row: that's when a straight is possible.
coach.math.look.reading: your own cards: they block your opponent's combos too.
coach.math.look.combos: cards on the board and in your hand that share ranks with the hand you're counting.
